whatItIs.heading: What is emergency water removal?
whatItIs.body: Emergency water removal is the immediate extraction of standing or actively flowing water from a home or structure to stop ongoing structural damage. It is the first physical intervention in a water damage event—before drying, before remediation, before any reconstruction. The service covers truck-mounted and portable high-volume extraction of standing water, safety isolation of electrical circuits in saturated areas, initial moisture mapping to identify how far water has migrated beyond visible surfaces, and the removal of materials that cannot be saved. Emergency water removal is distinct from standard water extraction: the urgency is higher, the crew is dispatched immediately regardless of hour, and the goal is to arrest damage in progress rather than manage a completed event. Without it, every additional hour costs more in structural saturation, mold risk, and insurance complications.

process.heading: How Gallagher handles emergency water removal

steps.title: Immediate dispatch—real person, any hour
steps.body: Call (951) 541-0034 and a live team member answers. No automated menu, no callback queue. Crew and equipment are dispatched immediately; typical on-site arrival is within 60 minutes across the five-county Southern California service area.

steps.title: Safety cutoffs and contamination assessment
steps.body: Before extraction begins, the crew isolates electrical circuits in affected zones and classifies the water—Category 1 (clean), Category 2 (gray water), or Category 3 (black water). Contamination category determines which materials can be saved and what safety protocols are required.

steps.title: High-volume extraction
steps.body: Professional-grade truck-mounted extractors remove the bulk of standing water quickly. Portable units reach areas trucks cannot access—bathrooms, closets, finished basements. Wet vacuums handle residual surface moisture on hard floors.

steps.title: Initial moisture mapping and handoff to drying
steps.body: Thermal imaging cameras and calibrated moisture meters identify water that has migrated into wall cavities, subfloor, and structural framing. This map becomes the baseline for the drying phase. The same crew transitions directly into structural dry-out—no scheduling gap.

signs.heading: Signs you need emergency water removal now

items.title: Visible standing water anywhere inside the structure
items.body: Any pooled water on floors—regardless of depth—is an emergency. Water follows the path of least resistance into subfloor, wall bases, and framing within minutes.

items.title: Active leak that cannot be shut off
items.body: A burst pipe, failed supply line, or overflowing fixture that is still running requires extraction to begin before or simultaneously with the plumber's repair. Waiting for the source to stop first costs hours.

items.title: Appliance failure flooding—water heater, washing machine, dishwasher
items.body: Appliance floods often release 30–50 gallons before the event is noticed. The water is typically Category 2 (gray water) and requires contamination-aware extraction protocols.

items.title: Roof leak during a storm with water entering through the ceiling
items.body: Storm-driven roof leaks can fill ceiling cavities before water becomes visible at the drywall surface. Once it breaks through, significant saturation has already occurred above.

items.title: Flooring that is spongy, warping, or separating at seams
items.body: Rapid structural change in flooring means water has already reached the subfloor. This is a delayed emergency—the window to save the subfloor is narrowing.

whyUs.heading: Why homeowners call Gallagher for emergency water removal
whyUs.body: The difference between a $1,200 job and a $9,000 job is often how fast extraction starts. Gallagher Restoration Co. is built around that reality. For more than 15 years, the company has run emergency water removal responses across Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange, San Diego, and Los Angeles counties—always with a live person answering the phone and a crew dispatched immediately. IICRC-trained technicians arrive with professional-grade extraction equipment, not residential wet-vacs. They classify contamination on arrival, which determines which materials are salvageable and what safety protocols protect your family. The crew that removes the water is the same crew that dries the structure and, if needed, handles reconstruction. Aaron and the team built the company on one-crew continuity because handoffs between separate mitigation and rebuild contractors are where jobs go wrong and homeowners lose time on claims.

pricing.heading: Emergency water removal pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Every job starts with a free on-site assessment—there is no charge to dispatch and diagnose. Emergency water removal in Southern California typically runs $400–$3,000 depending on the volume of water, the square footage affected, and the contamination category. The low end covers a contained clean-water event in a single room with fast-response extraction. The upper end reflects high-volume Category 2 or Category 3 events where contaminated water requires special handling, affected materials must be removed, and multiple rooms are involved. After-hours response does not carry a surcharge—the rate structure is the same at 2 a.m. as at 2 p.m. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents everything for your insurance carrier from the first minute on-site.

faqs.q: What should I do while waiting for the emergency water removal crew?
faqs.a: If it is safe to do so, shut off the water source and turn off electrical circuits in the affected area at the breaker. Move valuables and furniture off wet flooring if you can do so without standing in pooled water. Do not use a standard household vacuum to extract water—it creates an electrocution hazard and cannot remove enough volume to matter.

faqs.q: How fast can Gallagher Restoration get to my home in Southern California?
faqs.a: Gallagher Restoration Co. targets on-site arrival within 60 minutes across the five-county SoCal service area. Actual response time depends on your location within Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange, San Diego, or Los Angeles County and crew availability at the moment of the call.

faqs.q: Does Category 2 or gray water cost more to remove than clean water?
faqs.a: Yes, typically. Gray water—from appliances, sinks, or outdoor flooding—requires contamination-rated handling protocols, protective equipment, and antimicrobial treatment of affected surfaces. Black water events (sewage backups, outdoor flood water) add another tier of remediation requirements and cost.

faqs.q: Will my insurance cover emergency water removal?
faqs.a: Standard homeowners policies in California generally cover sudden and accidental water events—burst pipes, appliance failures, storm-driven roof leaks. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents cause, category, and scope on arrival and works directly with your adjuster throughout the claim.

faqs.q: What should I do if I discover water damage in my home?
faqs.a: First, shut off the water source if you can do so safely. Then document the damage with photos and video before anything is moved, and call a restoration professional or your insurance company. Do not use household vacuums or plug in appliances near standing water—that is an electrocution hazard.

faqs.q: Can water damage affect the electrical system in my home?
faqs.a: Yes. Water in walls, ceilings, or floors can reach outlets, junction boxes, and appliance circuits and create serious electrocution and fire hazards. If you suspect water damage near any electrical components, cut power at the breaker for the affected zone and consult an electrician before restoring the circuit.
